To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the determination of selenium compounds by hyphenated techniques, such as HPLC-ICP-MS, HPLC-ESI-MS, or LC-ESI-FT-ICR-MS, is a very promising approach for the determination of selenium species in biological samples and (ii) the identification of the detected species by these techniques is still a challenging task.

the determination of the selenium compounds in biological matrices is possible with a high degree of selectivity and specificity by the use of a combination of a separation technique and an element-specific detection technique.
the determination of selenium species is feasible by the application of a combination of techniques, but that the identification of selenium species is still not feasible.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new analytical technique for the determination of the species of selenium in living organisms.
the development of analytical techniques that are able to determine the species of selenium in living organisms in a species-selective manner.
the development and evaluation of new analytical methods for the selective determination and identification of selenium compounds in living organisms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the determination of the selenium species in living materials has not yet reached a state where a reliable and routine analysis is possible.
there is no technique available that is able to identify and characterize the various selenium species in a living organism.

, although the determination of selenium in living organisms has been a topic of interest for many decades and although a number of techniques have been developed to determine the selenium content of living organisms, only a few of them have been able to determine the selenium species present in living organisms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

there are a large number of techniques that are able to determine the total amount of selenium in biological materials, and there are a large variety of techniques that are capable of determining the total amount of selenoproteins in biological samples.

the analytical techniques currently available for the selective determination of selenium compounds are not sufficiently sensitive to allow for the determination of selenium species at trace levels in biological materials.
we have demonstrated the feasibility of the identification and the determination of various selenium compounds in living organisms using a combination of HPLC and AAS.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the development of a method that allows the identification of selenium compounds in complex biological matrices is a challenging task.
, in order to be able to identify the selenium species, the use of element-selective detectors is not sufficient, but that the use of a chromatographic separation step is necessary.
, in general, there is no single technique that is able to detect and to characterize all the selenium species that are known or suspected to occur in living organisms.
